rejectedAsSealedWording.claim: Semantic facts are the primary fact tier for any language with a usable compiler or language service. Syntax-only is the portable floor and a declared degraded mode — not the default.
rejectedAsSealedWording.problem: This is a rebuttal of the escape-hatch conclusion, not a derivation that 'primary' is the unique right default for every supported language and every profile.

alternatives.name: Always-primary (document claim as written)
alternatives.summary: Every language with a compiler runs semantic extraction on the normal path by default
alternatives.verdict: overcorrects; couples all profiles to Program cost

alternatives.name: Co-equal tiers, requirement-driven
alternatives.summary: Syntax and semantic are peer layers; planner materializes the max quality required by selected rules/profile; Coverage records shortfall
alternatives.verdict: best mechanism model; avoids false 'primary' ontology

alternatives.name: Profile-default primary (recommended)
alternatives.summary: For languages with a sealed semantic provider: full/CI/architecture profiles default to requiring semantic-quality references; agent-fast/text profiles may select syntax or partial semantic with explicit Coverage. Languages without a provider: syntax is the only tier — labeled capability, not degraded shame.
alternatives.verdict: preserves greenfield ambition without forcing Program on every invocation

agent1Recommendation.sealCandidateWording: Semantic extraction is a first-class fact tier for languages with a maintained provider. Profile and rule requirements determine whether a run materializes semantic facts. Full/CI defaults for those languages require semantic-quality references for reachability and architecture packs. Syntax-only is the sole tier until a provider exists, and a declared reduced-quality mode when a profile opts out — never a silent fallback.
agent1Recommendation.mustNotSeal: Always-on Program construction for any language that merely has a compiler
dependsOn: R-2 declarative split against real schema

whatWouldChangeMyMind: Measurement that agent-fast profiles still need semantic resolution for acceptable FP rates on the real agent recipe set
A cheap incremental semantic provider that makes always-on cost negligible at 10k+ files
